_comment: The per-file table for the [KERN] tier (docs/03-content-pipeline.md §2, docs/02 Parts D1 and D5).
Two shapes. `items` names one file each, keyed by <repository>/<path inside it>, and is
right when a handful of pieces are wanted from a large repository. `groups` describes a
whole opus once — its genre, its concepts, a title pattern and a level — and lets the
importer fill in the individual pieces, because Chopin's first editions run to 191
solo-piano works and 191 hand-typed titles would be 191 chances to mistype one.
Everything here is data a human edited, so tools/content/import_kern.py trusts none of it:
the repository licence, the file's own Humdrum !!!YEM / !!!YEC rights records, the
!!!ODT / !!!PDT publication year and the !!!COM composer are all re-read from disk, and a
row whose stated publishedYear disagrees with the file is excluded rather than believed.
A piece whose level came from its group's default rather than from a judgement about that
piece is tagged `level-banded` in the catalog, so a guess never passes for a measurement.
Run 1 (P10, 2026-09-05): the ragtime tier, docs/02 D5 Stages 6-8, from craigsapp/joplin.
Run 2 (P10, 2026-09-06): the Chopin first editions from the Fryderyk Chopin Institute —
CC BY 4.0, so they need no --allow-nc at all, and they replace the two craigsapp Chopin
repositories that state no licence. The three unlicensed repositories never get rows.

joplin.name: A Digital Edition of Scott Joplin's Music (craigsapp/joplin)
joplin.editionNotes: Humdrum **kern edition by Craig Stuart Sapp, referenced against the first editions; converted to MusicXML here by tools/content/convert.py. CC BY-NC-SA 4.0: bundled only in the owner's personal build (docs/00 D10a).

chopin-first-editions.name: First Editions of Fryderyk Chopin's Music (NIFC / chopinscores.org)
chopin-first-editions.editionNotes: Humdrum encoding of the 19th-century first edition, made at the Fryderyk Chopin Institute for the Chopin Heritage in Open Access project. CC BY 4.0 — redistributable, so this needs no --allow-nc; the attribution is the source block.
chopin-first-editions._composers_comment: Keyed on the file's own !!!COM record. The importer reads the composer out of the file and looks the death year up here, because these editions state a publisher and a plate number but never a year. Eleven spellings appear across the 512 files — the publishers were French, German, English and Polish, and one encoder typed 'Chopipn' — so every spelling is listed rather than matched loosely: a name this table does not know still stops the import.
chopin-first-editions._publisher_comment: Where a work survives in several first editions, this order decides which one is imported: the German house first, which is the text most modern editions descend from, then the French and the English. An editorial choice, so it lives here.

skipOpus.003: Op. 3 is the Introduction and Polonaise brillante for cello and piano; the file is the piano part alone.
skipOpus.013: Op. 13, Fantasy on Polish Airs, is for piano and orchestra; the file is the piano part alone.
skipOpus.073: Op. 73 is the Rondo for two pianos; primo and secondo are separate files and neither stands alone.

chopin-first-editions._idSuffix_comment: The MuseTrainer library already holds amateur transcriptions of some of these pieces under the obvious ids — song.classical.chopin-prelude-op28-4, both Op. 9 nocturnes, the Op. 64 No. 2 waltz, the first Ballade. This suffix keeps the scholarly first edition beside them instead of colliding with them, and two editions of one piece is a feature: docs/00 D21 wants alternatives at every rung.

mustStayExcluded.beethoven-piano-sonatas: no LICENSE file and no licence statement anywhere in the repository — a bare edition, nothing granted. --allow-nc relaxes non-commercial, not silence.
mustStayExcluded.chopin-mazurkas: no LICENSE file and no licence statement anywhere in the repository.
mustStayExcluded.chopin-preludes: no LICENSE file; the .krn files carry a bare '!!!YEC: Copyright <year> by Craig Stuart Sapp' with no !!!YEM licence record — a copyright claim is the opposite of a grant.

absentFromSource.joplin/euphonic: docs/02 D5 Stage 8 names Euphonic Sounds (1909). craigsapp/joplin holds 47 rags and that is not one of them (checked 2026-09-05). Needs another source or another Stage 8 option.
absentFromSource.joplin/frog-legs: docs/02 D5 Stage 8 names James Scott's Frog Legs Rag. craigsapp/joplin is Joplin only.
absentFromSource.joplin/ragtime-nightingale: docs/02 D5 Stage 8 names Joseph Lamb's Ragtime Nightingale. craigsapp/joplin is Joplin only.
absentFromSource.scarlatti/K32-K9-K380: docs/02 D1 Stages 5 and 7 name Scarlatti K.32, K.9 and K.380. None of the three is among the 65 sonatas in craigsapp/scarlatti-keyboard-sonatas, and MutopiaProject holds only K.11, K.455 and K.491. The rung can be filled, but not with those numbers.

joplin/kern/entertainer.krn.title: The Entertainer
joplin/kern/entertainer.krn.subtitle: A Rag Time Two Step
joplin/kern/entertainer.krn.editionNotes: The complete original, marked 'Not fast.' — the docs/02 D5 Stage 6 option. The MuseTrainer edition of the same piece is song.ragtime.joplin-entertainer.

joplin/kern/peacherine.krn.title: Peacherine Rag
joplin/kern/peacherine.krn.editionNotes: Marked 'Not too fast.'; published by John Stark & Son, St. Louis.

joplin/kern/easywinners.krn.title: The Easy Winners
joplin/kern/easywinners.krn.subtitle: A Rag Time Two Step
joplin/kern/easywinners.krn.editionNotes: Marked 'Not fast.'; four strains in A flat with a trio.

joplin/kern/mapleleaf.krn.title: Maple Leaf Rag
joplin/kern/mapleleaf.krn.editionNotes: Marked 'Tempo di marcia'; the rag that made Joplin's name. The MuseTrainer edition of the same piece is song.ragtime.joplin-maple-leaf-rag.

joplin/kern/solace.krn.title: Solace
joplin/kern/solace.krn.subtitle: A Mexican Serenade
joplin/kern/solace.krn.editionNotes: Marked 'Very slow march time'; a habanera rather than a rag, and the gentlest thing in this set — the easiest way into the style if the leaps of Maple Leaf are still too much.

joplin/kern/bethena.krn.title: Bethena
joplin/kern/bethena.krn.subtitle: A Concert Waltz
joplin/kern/bethena.krn.editionNotes: Marked 'Valse Tempo'; five strains in 3/4 with a key change at each — long (164 bars), but no faster than the two-steps.

joplin/kern/elite.krn.title: Elite Syncopations
joplin/kern/elite.krn.editionNotes: Secondary rag (a three-note figure against the four-note beat) in the third strain.

joplin/kern/pineapple.krn.title: Pine Apple Rag
joplin/kern/pineapple.krn.editionNotes: Marked 'Slow March tempo. [quarter]=100'; the tempo is Joplin's own, printed on the first edition.

joplin/kern/lilyqueen.krn.title: Lily Queen, Ragtime Two-Step
joplin/kern/lilyqueen.krn.editionNotes: Often catalogued as a collaboration with Arthur Marshall; this edition credits Joplin alone, so the catalog does too.

joplin/kern/school.krn.title: School of Ragtime
joplin/kern/school.krn.subtitle: Six Exercises for Piano
joplin/kern/school.krn.editionNotes: Joplin's own ragtime method: six short exercises, each one syncopation figure against a steady bass. The best possible way into the style.

joplin/kern/stoptime.krn.title: Stoptime Rag
joplin/kern/stoptime.krn.editionNotes: Joplin asks the player to stamp the heel on the floor through the stop-time breaks; the printed instruction is part of the piece.

007.skip: music21 cannot export it: the cadenza in bar 27 is a 29-in-24 tuplet whose base value is a 2048th note, and MusicXML stops at 1024th. Quantising it would change the music, so the piece is left out rather than altered. Import your own copy if you want it.

checkedAndRefused._comment: Humdrum collections looked at and turned down, with the reason, so nobody spends an afternoon rediscovering them. Found through humdrum-tools/humdrum-data, which indexes 75 collections; the piano-relevant ones are listed here.
checkedAndRefused.humdrum-tools/bach-wtc: 96 files, the Well-Tempered Clavier. No LICENSE, and every file carries '!!!YEM: Rights to all derivative electronic formats reserved.' — an explicit reservation, the opposite of a grant. docs/03 §2 asked whether a WTC kern edition existed under craigsapp; it exists under humdrum-tools and cannot be used.
checkedAndRefused.humdrum-tools/inventions: 30 files, the Two- and Three-Part Inventions, same David Huron encoding and the same reservation. docs/02 D1 Stage 7 wants Inventions 1, 4, 8 and 13 — they will have to come from [PDMX] or [MUTO].
checkedAndRefused.craigsapp/hummel-preludes: 24 preludes, Op. 67. No LICENSE and a bare '!!!YEC: Copyright 2008 by Craig Stuart Sapp' — the chopin-preludes shape.
checkedAndRefused.craigsapp/art-of-the-fugue: 20 files, no LICENSE and no rights record at all.
checkedAndRefused.ccarh/essen-folksong-collection: 8,473 folk melodies — single-line, so not piano scores, and the CCARH terms speak of a licensing agreement rather than a public licence. Not read in full; would need a proper look before use.
